title: D (programming language)
text:
Editors and integrated development environments (IDEs) supporting syntax highlighting and partial code completion for the language include SlickEdit, Emacs, vim, SciTE, Smultron, Zeus,[1] and Geany among others.[2]

Dexed (formerly Coedit),[3] a D focused graphical IDE written in Object Pascal

Mono-D[4] is a feature rich cross-platform D focused graphical IDE based on MonoDevelop / Xamarin Studio, mainly written in C Sharp.[5]

Eclipse plug-ins for D include DDT[6] and Descent (dead project).[7]

Visual Studio integration is provided by VisualD.[8,9]

Visual Studio Code integration with extensions as Dlang-Vscode[10] or Code-D.[11]

A bundle is available for TextMate, and the Code::Blocks IDE includes partial support for the language. However, standard IDE features such as code completion or refactoring are not yet available, though they do work partially in Code::Blocks (due to D's similarity to C).

The Xcode 3 plugin "D for Xcode" enables D-based projects and development.[12]

KDevelop (as well as its text editor backend, Kate) autocompletion plugin is available.[13]

Dlang IDE is a cross-platform IDE written in D using DlangUI library.[14]

Open source D IDEs for Windows exist, some written in D, such as Poseidon,[15] D-IDE,[16] and Entice Designer.[17]

D applications can be debugged using any C/C++ debugger, like GNU Debugger (GDB) or WinDbg, although support for various D-specific language features is extremely limited. On Windows, D programs can be debugged using Ddbg, or Microsoft debugging tools (WinDBG and Visual Studio), after having converted the debug information using cv2pdb. The ZeroBUGS debugger for Linux has experimental support for the D language. Ddbg can be used with various IDEs or from the command line; ZeroBUGS has its own graphical user interface (GUI).

DustMite is a tool for minimizing D source code, useful when finding compiler or tests issues.[18]

dub is a popular package and build manager for D applications and libraries, and is often integrated into IDE support.[19]
